page: Microsoft Azure E192s_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Esv7 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 192 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 96 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The system architecture is x86_64 and includes 1536.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or onboard GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance across multi-threaded computational workloads. The server achieves a top-tier rating in multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng and PassMark CPU evaluations, supported by a large 480 MB L3 cache and advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions. Memory subsystem performance is highly rated, with cached read bandwidth reaching 15010.89 GB/sec and uncached large-block read bandwidth at 688.47 GB/sec. Database operations and Redis SET benchmarks also place in the top tier, registering 251.49 million operations per second for Redis.

While multi-threaded throughput and memory bandwidth are exceptional, single-core performance is moderate, as evidenced by average ratings in single-core stress-ng tests. Additionally, despite strong prompt processing capabilities for large language models, text generation speeds are average to weak, particularly for smaller models. Given the high memory capacity, dedicated vCPUs, and lack of local storage, this server is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-intensive enterprise workloads that leverage external premium storage. It is highly suited for large-scale relational databases, in-memory caching layers, enterprise resource planning systems, and heavy multi-threaded data processing.
